title: Vet in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Every vet in Germany bills from one fee schedule, the GOT.** A practice charges **one to three times** the listed fee, plus **19% VAT**, with medicine on its own line.
**A general examination for a dog or cat is listed at €23.62**, so a quick look during opening hours costs **€28 to €84** including VAT. For a rabbit or guinea pig the listed fee is €15.39.

**The emergency service runs nights from 18:00 to 08:00, weekends from Friday 18:00 to Monday 08:00, and public holidays all day.** Then the range moves to **two to four times** the fee plus a flat **€50 emergency fee**.
**Opening hours beat the clock.** If your practice is open until 20:00, a visit at 19:30 is billed at normal rates, even though the fee schedule already counts it as night.
**The same limping dog with sedation and two X-rays costs €115 to €344 on a Monday morning and €289 to €519 on a Saturday night.** For small pets the €50 fee is larger than the examination itself.
**Five Berlin clinics and practices run a 24-hour small-animal emergency service**, in Biesdorf, Zehlendorf, Wilmersdorf, Reinickendorf and Marzahn. Save the nearest number before you need it.

**Breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, collapse, poison or a swollen belly in a dog means go now.** For everything else, call first: the clinic will tell you whether it can wait until your practice opens.
